original_source.title: Windows 11 - Flight Search Results - Carry-on filter hides eligible flights
original_source.preconditions: Clear browser cache/cookies; disable ad-blockers; enable DevTools Console with 'Preserve log' and 'Show timestamps'.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Open https://www.onetravel.com/
2. Click Flights.
3. Select One-way, 1 adult, and Economy.
4. Select Hanoi (HAN) as the origin and Ho Chi Minh City (SGN) as the destination.
5. Select November 16, 2026 as the departure date.
6. Click Done.
7. Click Search.
8. Click See Flights Only.
9. Click Select for the VietJet Air flight departing at 10:25 PM.
10. Scroll down to the Add Baggage section.
11. Click the browser's Back button to return to the flight search results.
12. Scroll down to the Baggage Included filter.
13. Select Carry-on bag.
14. Scroll down to the Airlines filter.
15. Click Show More.
original_source.expected_result: The VietJet Air flight departing at 10:25 PM (which explicitly states 'Carry-on baggage included' on the Review Trip Details / Add Baggage page) remains displayed in the search results and VietJet Air remains selectable under the Airlines filter after enabling the 'Carry-on bag' filter.
original_source.actual_result: After selecting the 'Carry-on bag' filter under Baggage Included, all VietJet Air flights (including the 10:25 PM flight confirmed to include carry-on baggage on its review page) disappear from the flight search results and from the Airlines filter list.

attachments.description: Highlighted screenshot showing VietJet Air flight card and Carry-on filter contradiction
Full flow screen recording from homepage without background noise
Chrome console log starting with '01:53:30.727 Navigated to https://www.onetravel.com/' with Preserve log and timestamps enabled across all 15 steps

review_outcome.ttl_reviewer_message:
Thanks for making the changes. However there are still a few mistakes in the report, please fix the mistakes listed below:
- Your log file does not contain the homepage URL. Please open the console and clear the log, refresh the homepage, and then save the log after you have reproduced the issue. Re-upload a new log afterward.
- Please capture a new console log from the first step of the action performed with selected 'preserve log' and 'enable timestamp' options. You should see a text line like '18:32:30.854 Navigated to'
Click 'Confirm all requested info is added' after you finish fixing your report.
- Upload a new log file, which covers all the steps of your actions performed from visiting the test URL to the issue page
review_outcome.resolution_notes: Resolved by keeping flight search in a single tab / capturing the initial 'Navigated to https://www.onetravel.com/' timestamped console log through `/air/listing` and `/air/review`, re-uploading, and clicking 'Confirm all requested info is added'. Subsequently Approved as Very Valuable.

agent_analysis.why_approved_high_value: Proved the defect using a concrete item (VietJet Air 10:25 PM flight HAN->SGN on Nov 16, 2026) whose Review/Detail page explicitly confirmed 'Carry-on included', then showed the listing filter ('Carry-on bag') excluded that exact item. Zero guesswork.
agent_analysis.why_ir_happened: OneTravel opened search results in a new tab (`target=_blank`), causing DevTools Console on Tab 2 to miss the Step 1 `Navigated to https://www.onetravel.com/` line.
agent_analysis.reproduction_complexity: 15 steps (requires visiting detail page first to prove eligibility in the video before applying the filter on the listing page).

inferred_lessons: Always anchor a filter bug on one specific item whose detail/review view proves it meets the filter criteria.

When a site opens search results in a new browser tab, DevTools on the new tab will miss the Step 1 homepage navigation line; force single-tab navigation or configure auto-open DevTools + preserve log from the homepage tab.

original_source.title: Windows 11 - Hotel Checkout - Advertised promo code 'OCTHTL' displayed directly on hotel card is rejected as 'not valid' at checkout
original_source.preconditions: Tested on 2026-10-29, prior to the advertised Oct 31, 2026 expiration date.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Open https://www.onetravel.com/
2. Click the Hotels tab.
3. Search for hotels in Merida, Mexico (MID) for check-in October 30, 2026 and check-out October 31, 2026.
4. Locate the hotel card 'Suites Reforma by Homirent' on the hotel search results page.

5. Click the info icon next to the green promo banner under the card ('Save instantly on your trip. Get up to USD 20.00 off select hotels. Use promo code OCTHTL at checkout' - 'Expires Oct 31, 2026').
6. Click Copy on the 'OCTHTL' promo banner.
7. Click Select on 'Suites Reforma by Homirent' and proceed to the Review your stay / Checkout page.
8. Expand 'Enter Promo Code' under Price Details.
9. Paste 'OCTHTL' into the Promo Code field.
10. Click Apply.
original_source.expected_result: The promo code 'OCTHTL' advertised directly on the 'Suites Reforma by Homirent' listing card (valid through Oct 31, 2026) is accepted and applies the qualified hotel discount at checkout.
original_source.actual_result: The checkout page rejects the promo code 'OCTHTL' with the red error message: 'Promo code is not valid, please try another code.'
original_source.error_message: Promo code is not valid, please try another code.

attachments.description: media_1793261675594_1129a727.png & media_1793261647793_a99e8aa3.png showing OCTHTL banner + tooltip on Suites Reforma by Homirent and rejection at checkout

review_outcome.resolution_notes: Confirmed via Mai's Cycle 562706 Tester Bugs Scorecard (3 Reported, 3 Approved: 1 Very Valuable, 2 Somewhat Valuable, 0 Rejected). Exact numeric uTest issue ID requires live authenticated issue list lookup.

agent_analysis.why_approved_high_value: Distinguished from general promo code 'OCT26' on flights (which returned 'The fare already includes our best available deal' = WAD). Because 'OCTHTL' was printed directly on the specific hotel card ('Suites Reforma by Homirent') with a visible tooltip ('Expires Oct 31, 2026'), rejecting it as 'not valid' on that exact hotel's checkout was an undeniable contradiction.
agent_analysis.reproduction_complexity: 10 steps from homepage to hotel checkout.

inferred_lessons: Compare error messages carefully: 'already includes our best available deal' is business logic (WAD), whereas 'Promo code is not valid' for a code printed directly on that item's card before its expiration date is a real functional bug.

review_outcome.final_status: New (at snapshot; Israell Valdes had 2 Approved, 1 Rejected on Scorecard)

normalized_fields.defect_category: Working as Designed / False Positive Risk (Flight Status Date Window)
normalized_fields.outcome_class: New / High WAD or Cannot Reproduce Risk

agent_analysis.why_approved_high_value: Real-time flight status trackers only allow selecting yesterday, today, or tomorrow by industry design; claiming 'Calendar Does Not Allow Flight Date Selection' with Critical severity when trying to pick far-future dates is a classic WAD/false-positive trap.

original_source.title: Windows 11 - Soft Triomphe Category - Editorial image covers four product tiles on en-vn locale
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Open https://www.celine.com/en-vn/
2. Navigate to the Soft Triomphe category product listing page (PLP).
3. Scroll through the product grid where the large editorial campaign image is placed.
original_source.expected_result: Product tiles and the editorial image render in separate grid cells without overlapping or obscuring product tiles.
original_source.actual_result: The editorial image in the Soft Triomphe category overlaps/covers four product tiles in the grid on en-vn.

attachments.description: Highlighted screenshot of editorial image covering four product tiles
Screen recording from homepage to Soft Triomphe category grid

review_outcome.ttl_reviewer_message: uTest status tooltip: Technically valid bug, but customer has no plan to fix it; avoid reporting similar issues for this product.
review_outcome.resolution_notes: Verified Approved (Won't Fix) in Cycle 562001 (documented in BUG_LESSONS.md #1 and MASTER_BUG_LIBRARY.md #5).

normalized_fields.defect_category: Luxury Editorial Grid Layout (Won't Fix Pattern)

agent_analysis.why_approved_high_value: Approved because 4 product tiles were obscured, but marked Won't Fix (WNF) because luxury fashion sites frequently use asymmetric editorial grid overlays and treat layout quirks as low-priority or intentional.

inferred_lessons: Approved (Won't Fix) is a warning signal: do not farm additional editorial grid/layout bugs on that product; pivot immediately to functional cart/filter/checkout mechanics.

original_source.title: Xiaomi 13 Pro - Search Results - 'OVER $50' filter displays discounted product priced below $50
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Open Chrome on the Xiaomi 13 Pro.
2. Navigate to https://www.maccosmetics.com/
3. Tap the Search icon.
4. Enter 'lipstick'.
5. Submit the search.
6. Tap 'FILTER & SORT'.
7. Select the 'OVER $50' filter.
original_source.expected_result: Only products with a current price over $50 are displayed after applying the 'OVER $50' filter.
original_source.actual_result: A product with a current sale price below $50, such as 'LIP COMBO BY @QUENBLACKWELL' priced at $36.40, is displayed after applying the 'OVER $50' filter.

attachments.description: Highlighted screenshot showing $36.40 product under OVER $50 filter
Remote debug mobile Chrome console log

review_outcome.ttl_reviewer_message: Corrected two practice-cycle mistakes: (1) removed standalone final step 'Observe...' and moved observation into Actual Results; (2) changed Source from Structured to Exploratory because the bug was found outside the test case steps.
review_outcome.resolution_notes: Documented in guidelines/utest_academy_handbook.md Section 8 & Section 9.1 (lines 244-291).

normalized_fields.defect_category: Sale Price vs Original Price Filter Mismatch

agent_analysis.why_approved_high_value: E-commerce price filters often filter against `original_price` ($52.00) instead of `current_sale_price` ($36.40), returning items that violate the user's selected price bracket.
agent_analysis.reproduction_complexity: 7 atomic steps (one action per step, no 'Observe' step).

inferred_lessons: On e-commerce sites with discounted/bundle items, test price filters ('Under $X', 'Over $Y') to see if backend filtering uses pre-discount price while UI displays sale price.
Never put 'Observe' as a numbered reproduction step; never select Source = Structured unless the bug directly occurred while executing a test case step.

original_source.title: Price Filter $400-$500 returns 0 products and hides filter controls, trapping user in unrecoverable empty state
original_source.expected_result: When a filter returns 0 results, the filter sidebar/chips remain visible so the user can uncheck or clear the filter.
original_source.actual_result: Selecting price filter $400-$500 returns 0 products and simultaneously hides the filter panel, leaving no UI control to remove the active filter.

review_outcome.resolution_notes: Preserved from BUG_LESSONS.md #6 as secondary community evidence.

agent_analysis.why_approved_high_value: An empty state (0 results) is NOT a bug by itself; it becomes a valid functional bug when the UI removes the Clear/Reset filter controls, trapping the user.

inferred_lessons: Never report '0 results found' alone; test whether the user can recover by clearing or unchecking the filter from the empty-state screen.

original_source.title: Review search keyword from previous product leaks into next product's reviews (showing 1/85 reviews)
original_source.expected_result: Navigating to a different product resets the review search/filter state.
original_source.actual_result: Review search keyword from Product A remains active on Product B, filtering Product B down to 1/85 reviews without a visible clear control.

review_outcome.resolution_notes: Preserved from BUG_LESSONS.md #7 as secondary community evidence.

agent_analysis.why_approved_high_value: SPA store failed to reset component filter state when route parameters changed from Product A to Product B.

inferred_lessons: Apply a sub-filter or search inside Entity A (e.g. hotel reviews, flight details), then navigate directly to Entity B and check if Entity A's filter leaked over.

original_source.title: Items in Account A cart remain visible after logging out and logging into Account B
original_source.expected_result: Account A's authenticated cart is isolated from Account B unless intentional guest-cart merge is documented.
original_source.actual_result: Items added under Account A remain in cart after logging out and signing into Account B.

review_outcome.resolution_notes: Preserved from BUG_LESSONS.md #8 as secondary community evidence.

normalized_fields.defect_category: Session / Cart Isolation vs Intentional Merge

agent_analysis.why_approved_high_value: Must distinguish intentional guest-cart merge on the same browser from actual cross-account data leakage.

inferred_lessons: Before reporting cart persistence across accounts, verify whether the item was added while logged into Account A (true session leak) vs added as a guest before login (often WAD cart merge).
